evals.name: planted-risks-forces-calibrated
evals.prompt: Can you do an architecture review of this repo? It's our family's app.
expected_behavior: Fills the forces checklist from the README (one household, one part-time developer, a $12 droplet) and marks each item stated or assumed
Flags secrets committed in docker-compose.yml (database and SMTP passwords) as a Blocker
Flags Postgres published on port 5432 to the internet with a weak password as a Blocker or Major
Flags Ruby 2.7 and Rails 6.0 as end-of-life runtime and framework, and Postgres 12 as end of life, at Major
Flags that the code uses Postgres while the accepted ADR-0001 says SQLite, as a decisions finding with Decision needed
Flags no backup or restore evidence as Unverified, and asks the user to run the matching ops-evidence commands rather than assuming
Notes deploy.sh has no rollback, judged against the forces at Minor, and does not recommend a staging environment or a service split
Ends by offering to grill decisions, export issues, or stop

evals.name: respects-007-adr-ownership
evals.prompt: Review this app's architecture and then grill me through any decisions so we can record ADRs.
expected_behavior: Notices .007-version and states that the architect agent owns ADRs in this repo
Delivers the full audit report first, then treats the prompt's request as the explicit yes and begins the grill without asking again
During the grill, asks one decision at a time with a recommended answer
Delivers each settled ADR as text in the section D format and writes nothing to docs/adr/
Tells the user to have the architect agent record each ADR in record mode

evals.name: real-app-full-review
evals.prompt: Run an architecture review of this app.
files: SUPPLY: a real single-server app repo
SUPPLY: output of the single-server and email sections of ops-evidence.md for its production server
expected_behavior: Builds a system map with the server, the database, the email provider, and any scheduled jobs, with a quantum count
Checks SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for the sending domain and bounce handling for the email provider
Reports every unrun ops check as Unverified with Low confidence
Every finding names a force and an evidence source

evals.name: no-config-asks-once
expected_behavior: Finds no .app-review.json and no tracker in Project knowledge, then asks once which tracker and target to use
Offers to save the answer as .app-review.json and writes it only on the user's OK
Puts handoff: code findings in the export queue with a handoff:code label, like any other finding
Does not ask about the tracker again later in the run
